html.<b>先に、走り続けないでください。</b> 500 のファンベルトは発電機と<: First, don't keep driving. The 500's fan belt turns both the generator and the cooling fan. The most common reason the charge lamp stays on is the belt, and if it has broken, the engine's cooling has stopped too. Stop somewhere safe, switch off, open the engine lid and check by eye that the belt is on, not broken and not loose. If it's broken, stop driving (running without cooling will seize the engine). If the belt is fine, read on.
html.<b>右の道を充電の電気がバッテリーへ戻っていく</b>のも見えます。戻る理由：: You can also see the charging current going back to the battery along the right-hand path. Why it goes back: while charging, the dynamo side is at a higher voltage than the battery, and current flows from higher to lower. The cut-out is the door that “opens this return path once charging starts, and disconnects it when charging stops (so the battery doesn't flow out backwards)”.

html.<span class=\"qa-h\">よくある疑問</span>カットアウト: A common question Even after the cut-out closes, the path to the lamp is still connected. It still doesn't light (and nothing flows backwards) because the upper and lower sides of the lamp are tied together and become the same point at the same voltage — just as water doesn't move between two ponds at the same level, with no difference nothing flows either way. “But while charging, isn't the dynamo side higher?” — that difference is used up along the heavy charging path (contact → wiring → battery). The lamp just joins the same two points in parallel with the closed contact, and the closed contact is a near-0Ω shortcut = it shorts out the bulb beside it, so the lamp sees only a few tens of mV (orders of magnitude too little to light). Conversely, if a badly adjusted regulator makes the charging voltage wobble and a difference appears, the lamp can glow faintly (that's what the “faint glow” symptom is).

Staying lit at idle is normal; if it goes out when you open the throttle a little, charging has started. ⚠️ If it doesn't go out well above that speed, suspect the four above in order.

html.ついでの疑問：「発電した電気がダイナモのアース（本体の取り付け）からそのまま車体: A side question: “Doesn't the generated current just escape into the body through the dynamo's ground (its mounting)?” — No. Current only flows around a loop that returns to its starting point; the body ground is just “shared wiring for the way back”. The dynamo's positive (+) side (51) is insulated from the body, so the only paths are through the battery and the electrical equipment. If the positive side touched the body directly, that would be a fault called a short.
